report:
Normal menisci, cruciate and collateral ligaments, popliteus musculotendinous unit, extensor tendons, and the distal iliotibial band. 
A subcentimeter midline femoral trochlear osteochondral lesion with no evidence of instability is demonstrated. No other associated extensor mechanism abnormality.  No marrow signal abnormality of concern, the remaining tricompartmental articular cartilage is well maintained throughout. 
No intra-articular loose bodies. Minimal intra-articular fluid, probably within normal physiological limits. Grossly unremarkable imaged extra-articular soft tissues.

MRI of Right Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

* Increase interstitial intensity of ACL and proximal PCL with straight linear contour suspect degenerative change
* Heterogenous hypertintensity and medial displacement(Srs:[ID] Img:9) of anterior horn of lateral meniscus with subcondromaedema(Srs [ID] Img:12) in the lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau suspect bucket handle tear 
* A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst.
* Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis. Mild deep infrapatellar and suprapatellar fat stranding; Wearing articular cartilage of femoral condyle
* Hyperintensity of popliteal muscle on F/S T2WI, suspect edema
* Honycombing hyperintensity in the subcutaneous layer of anterior knee on F/S T2WI suspect edema
* Fusiform dilatation of branches of popliteal vein(Srs:[ID]:15-19) in the posterior medial aspect of knee joint, cause to be determined
* A 14mm x 9mm x 15mm in size, well-defined, and oval-shpaed lesion in the subcutaneous layer of lateroanterior aspect of knee joint(Srs: [ID]: 13) showed mild hyperintensity on F/S T2WI and F/S PD, hypo- to isointensity on T1WI, suspect focal fat necrosis or small subcutanoue nodule.
> Prescence of anterior and posterior meniscofemoral ligaments
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of  grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration.

Impression:
1. Suspect bucket handle tear of anterior horn of lateral meniscus; degeneration of medial meniscus 
2. Osteoarthritis of right knee joint, more severe at lateral compartment with synovitis, suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae.
3. Baker's cyst formation 
4. Fusiform dilatation of branches of popliteal vein in the posterior medial aspect of knee joint, R/O venous insufficiency.
5. Bone marrow edema of lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau, maybe due to degeneration with subchondral edema; differential diagnosis of bone contusion.
6. Suspect  popliteal muscle edema
6. Suspect degenerative change of ACL and PCL
7. Subcutaneous edema of anterior knee 
8. A 14mm x 9mm x 15mm lesion in the subcutaneous layer of lateroanterior aspect of knee joint R/O focal fat necrosis or small subcutanoue nodule.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

MRI RIGHT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Right knee instability. Anterior drawer test positive? Anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
None

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: intact

Medial meniscus: Mild hyperintensity is seen at the posterior horn suggestive of intrasubstance degeneration. No definite tear. No parameniscal cyst. 

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: Intact fibers are present however caliber of these fibers is somewhat attenuated compatible with a remote low-grade partial thickness injury. No significant tibial translation.

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. No Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Marked patella chondral hypertrophy is seen measuring up to 1.0 cm in thickness at the patella apex. It appears heterogeneously hyperintense with regions of hypointensity, possibly due to mineralization. No evidence of invasion into the patella bone. It is closely abutting a medial plica. A possible loose body is also seen. Suspicious fissure also observed at the apex. Findings non specific in nature but favours to represent severe chondromalacia. Differential diagnoses such as focal synovitis and PVNS are less probable. 

Medial compartment: Mild chondrosis of the medial femoral condyle.

Lateral compartment: Mild chondrosis of the lateral femoral condyle.

Others:

Hoffas fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Low grade, remote, partial thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. No tibial translation.

Marked heterogeneous hypertrophy of the articular cartilage of the patella measuring up to 1.0 cm in thickness at the patella apex. Signal in this irregular thickened cartilage is heterogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted imaging and shows focal regions of hypointensity which may represent mineralization. Findings are favored to represent severe chondropathic change involving the articular cartilage of the patella.
